title: SQLite WAL commit tags and database snapshots
summary: Commit is marked when the number of database pages in the WAL frame header is non-zero; frames before the commit record can together constitute a transaction.
applies: SQLite 3 master database and WAL files
detail: Looking only at the master database file may be missing committed changes that have not yet been checkpointed. To interpret a snapshot, confirm that the WAL belongs to the same set of files as the main library.
boundary: Valid frames at the end of the file may also belong to uncommitted transactions; all frames cannot be considered final.
relevance: Explains why reading the main file directly can show different records from opening the database with its WAL present.
